A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ε-VAE research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Content can be reliably matched across the title, pagination, and table-numbering changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original ImageNet and COCO reconstruction results, image-generation experiments, and architecture, loss, compression, and sampling analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds one-step reconstruction, higher-compression generation, and classifier-free-guidance results.

M1.justification: The latent-conditioned diffusion decoder, velocity objective, perceptual and trajectory-matching losses, and noise/time schedules remain unchanged. One-step decoding was already supported; v4 adds evaluations of that existing capability.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet for reconstruction and conditional/unconditional generation, and COCO-2017 for reconstruction. The added experiments vary compression, decoding steps, and guidance within these existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds MaskGIT to the 16×16 ImageNet reconstruction comparison, with rFID 2.28, and ViT-VQGAN to the 8×8 comparison, with rFID 1.28. All previously reported comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V4 adds one-step 8×8 reconstruction comparisons using Base and Medium models, 32×32 class-conditional generation, and 8×8 generation with classifier-free guidance. Existing splits, training budgets, and quality metrics remain unchanged; the additions do not establish reruns of existing experiments.

E4.justification: The dedicated one-step comparison and guided-generation experiment extend checks of decoding efficiency and whether the generation advantage persists under guidance. Existing architecture, conditioning, loss, scheduling, scaling, and resolution analyses are retained. The new explanation of Figure 3 interprets unchanged plotted results.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains the same qualitative examples with varying reconstruction seeds. Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests, and v4 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing matched quality scores are retained. New Table 3 reports one-step rFID 0.57/0.51 for ε-VAE-SD B/M. Table 4 adds 32×32 generation FID 21.31/15.98/14.26 for SD-VAE/ε-VAE-SD M/H; Table 10 adds guided FID 3.51/2.83/2.69 for those methods. Retained throughput numerals are relabeled from image/sec to image/ks, revising their reported units without establishing changed runtime.

T1.justification: No formal definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs change. V2's explicit conditional velocity-loss equation is replaced by an equivalent reference to Equation 6 with the conditioning substitution explained in prose. Subsequent equation renumbering does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims about reconstruction, generation, few-step efficiency, and resolution generalization are retained. V4's abstract explicitly distinguishes quality gains at fixed compression from speed gains at increased compression, a distinction already stated in v2's introduction.

C2.justification: V4 adds a potential objective-bias caveat and an argument that latent conditioning mitigates it, explains degradation beyond three decoding steps, and expands discussion of computation/fidelity tradeoffs and higher-compression efficiency. These extend the retained limitations and interpretations in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same architecture specifications, loss weights, optimizer settings, training budgets, augmentation, software, and hardware disclosures. No code/data access information or additional implementation recipe is supplied for the new evaluations; the guided experiment does not specify a guidance scale.

R1.justification: V4 adds Lee et al. (2023) in Appendix B to distinguish encoded initial noise from latent conditioning, and Sargent et al. (2025) in Section 3.2 as a future decoder-fine-tuning direction. Existing positioning against diffusion autoencoders, SWYCC, and DiTo remains.

P1.justification: The title and headers spell out Epsilon-VAE, the publication footer is updated, and localized explanatory paragraphs and copyedits are added. Most prose and the overall section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables 3 and 10, expands Table 2 and the former Table 3, and revises the throughput heading. Figure 3's right panel has a corrected legend and slight sizing changes, with unchanged data. Other figures are retained, with table renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The one-step, higher-compression, and guided comparisons provide useful additional support for practical efficiency and generation quality, while the bias and few-step discussions improve qualification of the method. These are limited gains to an otherwise stable paper. The guided experiment remains under-specified and conflicts with Appendix C.3's retained blanket statement that guidance is never used.
